plan.title: A founder asks for a vague next step for a tester with two goals; ZOH asks which goal and how before filing

context.text: Ten days in a row, Jordan. Toast legs are earned legs 🏃

transcript.text: Stamati: he's doing great, bump him up a level
Do you mean a harder run, like longer or more days (an upgrade), or adding a new goal on top? He's already at Pushy, the top coaching level, so it can't go higher. Tell me which and I'll draft it.
Stamati: the running. make it a harder version, intervals instead of a steady run

[draft card: Do it / Change / Cancel] File a next step for Jordan (upgrade on Get fitter): "Swap the steady 20 minute run for a 20 minute interval run at the park, same days and time (7 am Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat), same screenshot proof from the run app summary.". ZOH raises it as its own idea when it fits, and asks first.

The draft is on your screen. If you click Do it, ZOH will offer Jordan intervals in place of the steady 20 minute run. The days, time and screenshot proof stay the same. ZOH brings it up when it fits, and Jordan decides.

conversation.reason: ZOH 2's draft card states the exact filing and what Jordan will be offered, and ZOH 3 says it will offer intervals in place of the run without claiming anything is filed.
ZOH 1 asked whether Stamati meant an upgrade or a new goal before drafting, and ZOH 2 names the goal (Get fitter) once he said running and intervals, though ZOH 1 never explicitly asked which goal.
It did not file on the ambiguous 'bump him up a level', asked which kind of change, then drafted an upgrade on the exercise goal and said it wasn't filed; it asked which goal only implicitly.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the ambiguous 'bump him up a level' well: it held off on filing, asked Stamati what kind of change he meant, then drafted the interval upgrade on the exercise goal with an accurate 'draft on your screen, not filed' line. The only soft spot is that it never explicitly asked which goal, relying on running being the focus goal.
